catalogue_scope: A curated public reading map across the author-published archive. The provider archive remains the authority for its current listing.
verification_status: Direct author-published Substack links. They are public research commentary, not peer-reviewed publications, independent validation, engineering proof, commercial-performance evidence, or investment evidence.

themes.label: Orientation
themes.description: Start with the programme map, scope and author-stated evidence standard.
themes.prompt: Use this note to understand the reading order, scope or evidence language before assessing individual propositions.

themes.label: Evidence methods
themes.description: Falsifiability, reproducibility, null models and cross-field tests.
themes.prompt: Ask what would reproduce, falsify or stop the claim, and whether the proposed test is independent of the model.

themes.label: AI & data
themes.description: Inspectable signals, AI behaviour and data-led observatories.
themes.prompt: Separate an observed pattern or interface behaviour from a validated system capability or outcome.

themes.label: Frontier systems
themes.description: Early-stage architectures spanning propulsion, photonics and protection.
themes.prompt: Look for the inherited engineering baseline, the missing measurement and the next bounded experiment.

themes.label: Space & sensing
themes.description: Orbital patterns, signals, debris protection and remote sensing.
themes.prompt: Check the reference dataset, control case and non-detection before treating a pattern as a prediction.

themes.label: Earth & history
themes.description: Geology, landscape evidence and long-horizon historical interpretation.
themes.prompt: Keep physical evidence, chronology and cultural resemblance separate until a supported connection exists.

themes.label: Biology & coherence
themes.description: Emerging biomolecular, fungal and biological-signal questions.
themes.prompt: Start with the public dataset and locked protocol; publication of a proposed signal is not evidence that the signal exists.
